newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold closes marginally firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: HK gold closes marginally firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed marginally firmer on Monday after trading within a 30 U.S. cent range in an extremely quiet session due to market holidays in Tokyo and London, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$340.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$339.95/340.45 close on Friday and Saturday's local close of US$340.00/50.

"The local market has been very quiet, with small amounts of short-covering interest," a bullion dealer said. "Gold remains stuck within a range and is likely to continue thus with resistance at US$342 and support at US$338."
Local gold ended HK$5 higher at HK$3,153 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -4.00 from its previous fix at -3.50.
